verdict.rationale: GitBook documents its own public API reference, describing a RESTful API that supports GET, POST, PATCH and DELETE, so the product itself offers a documented programmatic interface. The evidence is a single line, though. It does not show which resources or actions the API can drive, how authentication works, or any rate limits, and probes found no machine-readable OpenAPI spec at the common paths. The MCP server and CLI are separate interfaces and are not credited here. Missing for 10: documented endpoint scope showing that core product actions (spaces, pages, sites, change requests) can be driven through the API, authentication and token documentation, a published OpenAPI spec, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: This API is RESTful and supports standard HTTP methods like GET, POST, PATCH, and DELETE.
